_: Every judgement call the capture could not make for itself, in ONE file, so that
Mustafa's answers are an edit here rather than a rewrite of map.mjs.
`confirmed: false` is load-bearing: map.mjs REFUSES to emit a payload while any
decision it actually uses is unconfirmed, unless --allow-unconfirmed is passed. A
guess that silently becomes a menu is the failure this file exists to prevent —
four of these groups, read literally, would force every guest to remove an
ingredient before they could order.
Questions and their numbering: docs/tenants/mcfood/mustafa-questions.md (workspace,
gitignored — it holds the partner's email address).
Their model is ONE flat 'modifier group' primitive. Ours deliberately splits that
across three mechanisms (src/types/menu/sauce.ts: 'deliberately NOT a general
min/max-select engine'). `target` says which mechanism each group becomes:
sauceRule   -> Product.SauceMin/Max/IncludedFree + kind:'sauce' ingredient rows
ingredients -> ProductIngredient[] (isOptional / price / isIncludedInBasePrice)
bundle      -> MenuDefinition + MenuSection, ProductType 'menu'  [NOT YET BUILT]
OWNER RULING 2026-09-03, and it changed the mapping rather than just confirming it:
1. There are NO 'Sans X' records. A removal is not a thing to add — it is the
INGREDIENT, marked optional and included in the base price, which the guest
unticks. So 'Sans Salade' becomes the ingredient `Salade`. Emitting a row
literally named 'Sans Salade' would have shown a checkbox the guest ticks in
order to NOT have something: a double negative on every product.
2. Every group their data marks `isRequired: false` IS optional. Their
`minSelect: 1` is ignored wherever it contradicts that — which is all seven.
`displayName` now only reaches a guest for a BUNDLE group (a MenuSection heading).
Ingredient rows carry no group heading, because exclusionGroup is null on all of them.
